# v1.0.1 — Lock In Launcher

- Adds a separate, generally themed Lock In Launcher with an app library,
  verified updates/repair, release notes and download progress.
- Quiz opens directly. Create a direct shortcut from the launcher or choose
  the additional direct Quiz shortcut during Windows setup.
- The launcher starts independently of Quiz files and saved data, so repair
  remains available when Quiz cannot open. Existing saves and private dev
  profile isolation are retained.
- Download the separate Windows or Mac Launcher, then choose **Download** for
  Quiz. Windows uses separate installers; Mac has separate Apple Silicon and
  Intel DMGs for each app. Drag each Mac app into Applications.
- The Launcher reads only the public current-version manifest. It needs no
  private-repo login or token. Previous downloads are retained privately and
  removed from the public repository; no application source is public.
- Progression saves use authenticated encryption tied to the computer and OS
  account. Edited/replayed currency, inventory and quiz progress are rejected;
  startup recovery can restore the last verified save while preserving suspect
  files. Public and development saves use separate keys.
- Backups restore on the same installation only and retain the latest trusted
  wallet, inventory and cases. They do not contain recovery keys. Keep the OS
  account and secure-storage records; a data-folder copy does not transfer them.
- Before this first external distribution, private source supports the owner's
  one-time legacy migration. Public builds start protected and reject planted
  plaintext progress. Offline protection deters editing; it cannot prevent a
  determined machine owner from modifying the program itself.

The existing private source repository remains unchanged. Approved build inputs,
fingerprints and native verification receipts are retained in the separate
private archive. Mac builds are ad-hoc signed rather than Developer ID signed or
notarized; macOS may require Privacy & Security > Open Anyway on first launch.
